pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: src/lib/report/compare.ts:505 The diff's 'ruler' identity is the rubric version alone, so two model-scored scans graded by different judge models (ComparableScan records engineModel, but no comparison reads it; MixedEngineCaveat only fires for mock vs live) are spliced into one delta without any discontinuity notice, which judge-stability forbids because the model is part of the instrument.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/report/compare.ts:505 Pins and annotates the rubric, but not the judge model; engineModel is on ComparableScan yet unused in compare.ts, WhatChanged or trends, so a model swap between live scans is spliced silently.
src/components/report/WhatChanged.tsx:40 When the exam (rubric) changed underneath, the comparison says so before showing deltas, instead of presenting rubric movement as improvement.
src/lib/report/compare.ts:308 A score movement is attributed to judgment drift rather than to invented evidence when no detector signal changed (the signalDelta is kept separately).
src/components/report/TrendChart.tsx:102 Points from the deterministic floor are drawn differently and footnoted, so a no-model score is labelled as what it saw rather than plotted as a model grade.

declined.reason: This context meters scans, tokens and estimated LLM cost for billing (src/lib/db/usage.ts:1). It does not compare arms or score candidates, so eval-harness does not govern it (cost-metering does). I can't mark it not-applicable safely: its src/lib/db directory contains 'harness', 'benchmark' and 'scenario' in unrelated files, and the driver's absence search would fail.
